title: Morning puja
hook: the whole thing in four minutes

segments.voice: Yesterday, naivedya, the sweet that goes to the shrine first. Your line was shared.

People sometimes imagine puja as a long, complicated ceremony that only a priest can run. At a temple on a festival day, it can be. At home, on a Tuesday, before work, it can be four minutes. This week you've laid out the pieces like parts of a watch: a corner and five objects. One flame, the lamp. A flower, fresh, daily. A bell that helps you arrive. Water: washed, given, received. And a sweet that goes to the shrine first and comes back to be shared. Today, the watch goes together.
screen: `NOT JUST FOR PRIESTS.` → `A WEEK OF PIECES.` → `TODAY: PUT IT TOGETHER.`

segments.voice: Puja, your word from day eight, means honoring, worship, and that day's line still holds: attention is an offering. Full temple worship can have sixteen services, the whole welcome of a royal guest. Many homes use a short form, and old manuals even name a five-part version: fragrance, flower, incense, lamp and food. Your week covered three of those five, the flower, the lamp and the food, and added a bell and water. So here's one simple morning shape. Families do it in different orders, and none is the only right one. Begin clean: wash, or sip a little water. Ring the bell, and let it bring you here. Light the lamp. Offer a flower and a few drops of water. Set down something sweet. Then the heart of it: a few moments of mantra, Om, or the one from the mantra days that fits you, Om namah shivaya or the Gayatri, or simply the name you honor, said quietly. Then pranam, the bow from day four: hands together, head down. Last, take a little of the sweet back as prasad, and share the rest later. Bell, lamp, flower, water, food, name, bow. Some mornings you'll do all of it. Some mornings you'll just light the lamp and bow, and that small version is attention given too. The point was never the full list. The point is that before the day grabs you, something else gets the first four minutes.
screen: `PUJA — ATTENTION IS AN OFFERING.` · `A FIVE-PART FORM FOR HOME.` · `BELL, LAMP, FLOWER, WATER, FOOD.` · `A NAME, A BOW, THE SWEET RETURNS.`

segments.voice: However small your corner is, even if it's only in your mind, go through it once: ring the bell or tap a glass and listen until it fades, light the lamp or picture it, then set down a flower or a leaf, a few drops of water and a small piece of something sweet. Quietly say your mantra or a name you honor a few times, if you'd like. Then put your hands together, bow, and sit in front of it for the rest of the time.
Morning puja. The home shrine, put together: bell, lamp, flower, water, food, a name and a bow, before the day begins. Today's word.
Your line: four minutes. Any version of it counts, even a lamp and a bow. Day one hundred seventeen, and that's the week.

howItsDone: Many Hindu households do a short daily puja at the home shrine in the morning: ringing a bell, lighting a lamp, offering flowers, water and food, saying a mantra or a deity's name, bowing, and sharing the offered food as prasad.
